docs.coated.component: `Coated` is a runtime layer mixed OVER a surface — the part `Surfaced`'s static record cannot
hold. A record is a style-sheet class every client agrees on; `Coated` is what changes at play
time, per instance, and it fits four cases the record cannot by construction.
```ts
import { node, Bounded, Surfaced, Coated, installStockCoats } from "game-kit"
installStockCoats()   // the recipes, and the effect that mixes them
const shard = node("manaShard",
Bounded(), Surfaced({ surface: "plate" }),
Coated({ self: { recipe: "wash", level: 0.6, tint: "accent" } }))
## The two fields, and the reach
`self` is the coat on THIS face; `cast` is the coat on this node and every descendant that has
not overridden it. The reach is not a branch — it is the field's inheritance CLASS. `self` is
`own`, so it stays put; `cast` is `fromOwner`, so it falls to the subtree. Freeze a tray and the
figures on it grey too, with nothing walking the tree.
The inversion — «everything EXCEPT this one» — falls out for free: cast a dim on the root and set
`cast` to the `clear` recipe on the lit subtree. Overriding an inherited value is exactly what a
spotlight is, so it needs no machinery of its own.
## Why a recipe name and not the pixels
Each field is a `Coat`: a recipe NAME, a `level`, a `tint`. The look lives in a registry, the
mirror of `surfaces` — `render/coats.ts`. The recipes differ by the KIND of mark, never by value:
there is no `darken` beside a `charge` beside a `dim`, only one `wash` told apart by the tint and
level handed to it. A changing magnitude is a PARAMETER, not a new record — the same lesson the
kit learned the hard way about a highlight colour once.
- `wash` — a flat colour over the surface, opacity from `level`. The continuum: a shard charging,
a figure dimming as it loses HP, a frozen tray greying its children.
- `ring` — a stroke around the contour, weight from `level`. A selection, a ward.
- `censor` — the face ground up into drifting motes, each the colour of what it hides.
- `clear` — nothing, but it stops the cast cascade at this node.
## The infinite palette
A colour there are infinitely many of stays a token. `tint` can be a parametric `{token, param}` —
`spin` is the hue wheel, and N runtime teams are one recipe name and N numbers, never N hexes and
never N records. The wire carries only names and numbers; the raw colour is born on the client.
## Shared, not per-viewer
A coat is SHARED state: it travels the wire and looks the same to everyone. The onlooker plane —
theme, reduce-motion — is neither shared nor on the wire, and the coat effect never reads it. A
private mark (a bluff only its placer sees) is a projected field the orchestrator omits from other
viewers' trees — an ABSENCE, not a visibility flag. Privacy never leaks into shared state because
it is not IN the shared tree to begin with.
## The mask and the honest boundary
`censor` names an OVERLAY — the filter registry's twin, and the second seam a coat can point at.
A filter reworks the pixels a quad already put on the glass; an overlay is handed a look at them
and builds its own objects on top, which is the only way a mote can carry the colour of the spot
it hides. Both travel the same way: the plan carries `{ name, params }` as plain data a test can
read, and the objects are built in the one file that owns the renderer.
What that file decides is kept to nothing: the grid, which cells are lit, the colour a mote
inherits and where it is at second `t` are all pure functions in `render/dust.ts`, held down by a
unit test. A name nobody registered is skipped, exactly as a dangling surface record is.
docs.coated.coat: One node wearing both coats at once. `self` is on this face; `cast` would fall to children too,
and on a lone node it lands on itself — so both are visible here.
Drag `selfLevel` and the wash creeps: a magnitude, not a scene per value. Switch `selfRecipe` to
`ring` and the same number thickens a border instead. Pick a `selfTint` and it recolours. This is
the whole atom on one panel — everything past this scene is an ASSEMBLY that shows one case.
docs.coated.cascade: A tray casts over the figures standing on it. `cast` is `fromOwner`, so the freeze greys the
children with no code walking the tree — take the tray's cast away and they clear.
Turn on `spotlight` and one figure clears the cast back to nothing. «All but this one» is a dim
on the tray and a `clear` on the lit child — the inversion is overriding an inherited value, not
a scope switch. There is no `if scope ===` anywhere in the kit; the reach is the class, and the
class already knows how to be overridden.
docs.coated.team: N runtime players, each tinting a tile its own hue. The wire carries ONE recipe name and N
numbers — never N hexes, never N records. `spin` is the hue wheel and the parameter is the seat.
Drag `count` and the spectrum divides evenly, however many arrive. This is the answer to «a
colour there are infinitely many of» under the token law: a token is a name plus a number, and
the raw colour is resolved on the client, so a colour-blind palette could remap the whole board
without a byte of the wire changing.
docs.coated.censor: The censorship case: the hidden face GROUND UP. Motes are born on the node's own silhouette, each
one carrying the colour of the spot it came from, drifting outwards and fading over its own short
life. A censored ace of spades still reads as an ace of spades, smeared.
The atom holds the static truth — `censor`, a strength — and the animation is the render tier's,
where the live per-object transform already lives. The model NAMES an overlay and the painter
draws it: a filter reworks pixels already on the glass, an overlay is handed a look at them and
builds its own things on top, which is the only way a mote can be the colour of what it hides.
docs.coated.bluff: TWO TREES side by side — the same card as two clients hold it. The bluffer's tree carries the tell

No recipe here reads a viewer, and none may: a coat is shared state that travels the wire, and the
onlooker plane is neither shared nor on the wire (`guard.coat-not-viewer`). Privacy is a field a
tree does not contain — never a flag the paint checks.
